2027-03-07.title: K'piphtho Sunday · The Healing of the Bent Woman
readings: I give you thanks, O Lord and King
The Lord has opened my ear
2027-03-07.alt: Fifth Sunday of the Great Fast.
2027-03-07.verse: Woman, you are set free from your ailment.
theo: In a synagogue on the sabbath there is a woman who “had a spirit that had crippled her for eighteen years. She was bent over and was quite unable to stand up straight.” For eighteen years she has looked only at the ground. Jesus sees her, calls her, and says: “Woman, you are set free from your ailment.” He lays his hands on her, “and immediately she stood up straight and began praising God.”

The leader of the synagogue is indignant: healing is work, and work is forbidden on the sabbath. Jesus answers: you untie your ox and donkey on the sabbath to give them water; “ought not this woman, a daughter of Abraham whom Satan bound for eighteen long years, be set free from this bondage on the sabbath day?” The sabbath is the day of God's rest, and God's rest is our freedom.

Many of us are bent: by guilt, by worry, by addiction, by years of carrying burdens alone, by sins we have stopped noticing. We get used to looking at the ground. The Fast is the time when Jesus calls us, lays his hands on us, and lets us stand straight again and look up to God.

The evening Gospel, the Good Samaritan, shows us how to be Christ's hands for others: “moved with pity”, he bound up the wounded man's wounds. St Paul says: “present your bodies as a living sacrifice… Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your minds… Rejoice with those who rejoice, weep with those who weep.” Healed ourselves, we become healers: “Go and do likewise.”
conn: A daughter of Abraham.
Jesus restores her dignity: not just a patient, but a daughter of the covenant, like Zacchaeus, “a son of Abraham” (Luke 19:9).
The Good Samaritan.
The Fathers saw Christ himself in the Samaritan: he came down to wounded humanity, poured oil and wine, and brought us to the inn of the Church.
The opened ear.
Isaiah 50:4–5: “Morning by morning he wakens my ear”; the servant of the Lord listens and does not turn back.
Blessing for evil.
1 Peter 3:9: “Do not repay evil for evil… but, on the contrary, repay with a blessing.”
altar: At every Holy Qurbono the Good Samaritan pours the oil and wine of his grace into our wounds. We leave the altar standing straighter, called to bend down to the wounded on our road.
outline: Eighteen years looking at the ground: what bends us?
He notices the one no one notices.
Point 2 · Set free on the sabbath
God's rest is our freedom; Sunday as a day of healing.
The Good Samaritan: be Christ's hands for the wounded.
live: Name what bends you
Bring one burden or habit to Jesus in Confession or prayer this week.
Be a Samaritan (Luke 10:37)
Stop for one person in need you would usually pass by.
Make Sunday a day of rest and healing
Keep Sunday for God, family and works of mercy.
fathers: St Augustine
The Samaritan is our Lord, who became our neighbour; he bound our wounds, set us on his own beast, and brought us to the inn, the Church, until he returns (Sermon 171; On Christian Doctrine I).
St Ambrose of Milan
The bent woman is an image of the soul bowed down to earthly things; Christ's hand raises it to look to heaven (Exposition of the Gospel of Luke 7).
magis: Catechism 2172–2173
The sabbath is a day of freedom from work and for the works of mercy; Jesus healed on the sabbath to show this.
Catechism 1825, 2447
Love of neighbour and the works of mercy, spiritual and corporal.
Fratelli Tutti 56–86
Pope Francis on the Good Samaritan: we are all called to stop and bend down to the wounded.
saints: 9 Mar: the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste. 14 Mar: Samio Sunday.
2027-03-07.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw the bent woman, called her, and set her free. Lay your hands on us in this Fast: lift what bends us down, let us stand straight and praise you, and make us Good Samaritans for the wounded on our road. Amen.

2027-03-14.title: Samio Sunday · The Healing of the Blind
readings: Solomon asks for an understanding mind
The Lord made the earth by his power
2027-03-14.alt: Sixth Sunday of the Great Fast. The Fortieth Day of the Fast is Friday 19 March; Lazarus Saturday is 20 March; Hosanna Sunday is 21 March: remind the faithful to bring palm leaves and flowers.
2027-03-14.verse: One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see.
theo: On the last Sunday before Holy Week the Church reads two healings of the blind. In John, Jesus meets a man blind from birth. The disciples ask whose sin caused it. Jesus answers: “Neither this man nor his parents sinned; he was born blind so that God's works might be revealed in him… As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.” He makes mud, anoints the man's eyes, and sends him: “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam (which means Sent).”

The healed man is questioned again and again by the Pharisees. He does not know all the theology, but he knows one thing: “Though I was blind, now I see.” Step by step his sight grows: first “the man called Jesus”, then “a prophet”, then, kneeling before him, “Lord, I believe.” Meanwhile those who claim to see become blind. Jesus says: “I came into this world for judgment so that those who do not see may see, and those who do see may become blind.”

In Mark, blind Bartimaeus sits by the road at Jericho and cries out: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” People tell him to be quiet; he cries out louder. Jesus asks: “What do you want me to do for you?” “My teacher, let me see again.” “Go; your faith has made you well.” And Bartimaeus “followed him on the way”, the way to Jerusalem and the Cross.

Job, after all his suffering, says: “I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.” This is the goal of the Fast: not only to hear about God, but to see him with the eyes of faith. In Baptism, called “enlightenment” by the Fathers, we were washed and given sight. As Holy Week begins, let us ask with Bartimaeus: “Lord, let me see,” and then follow Jesus on the way.
conn: Siloam, “Sent”.
The man washes in the pool called Sent, and Jesus is the One sent by the Father: the Fathers saw here an image of Baptism, the washing that gives sight.
Clay and anointing.
Jesus makes clay as God formed Adam from the earth (Genesis 2:7): a new creation.
Solomon's prayer.
Solomon asked for an understanding mind (1 Kings 3:9); true sight is wisdom from God.
Following on the way.
Bartimaeus follows Jesus “on the way” to Jerusalem (Mark 10:52): healed disciples walk with him to the Cross.
altar: The Fathers called Baptism “illumination” and the Eucharist the food of those who see. At the Holy Qurbono we pray with Bartimaeus: “Have mercy on us”, and we receive the Light of the world.
outline: What is the worst kind of blindness?
Jesus opens eyes: new creation, Siloam, Baptism.
From “a man called Jesus” to “Lord, I believe”.
Point 3 · Those who think they see
Bartimaeus: cry out, receive sight, follow to Jerusalem.
live: Pray Bartimaeus' prayer
Repeat during the day: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.”
Prepare for Holy Week
Bring palm leaves and flowers on Sunday; plan to attend the services of Holy Week.
Honest measures (Deuteronomy 25:13)
Examine honesty in business, weights, wages and taxes.
fathers: St Augustine
The man born blind is the human race; the clay is the Word made flesh; the washing in Siloam is Baptism, by which we are enlightened (Tractates on John 44).
St Ephrem the Syrian
With the clay he formed eyes as he had formed Adam from the dust; the Creator showed himself in the creating hand (Commentary on the Diatessaron).
magis: Catechism 1216
Baptism is called “enlightenment”, because those who receive it are enlightened in their understanding.
Catechism 2616
Jesus hears the prayer of faith: “Son of David, have mercy on me”; the Jesus Prayer comes from such cries.
Lumen Fidei 1–4
Faith is a light that illumines every aspect of human existence.
saints: 17 Mar: St Patrick. 18 Mar: St Cyril of Jerusalem. 19 Mar: St Joseph, and in 2027 also the Fortieth Day of the Great Fast. 20 Mar: Lazarus Saturday.
2027-03-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, light of the world, you opened the eyes of the man born blind and of Bartimaeus. Have mercy on us: heal our blindness, let us see you with the eyes of faith, and give us grace to follow you on the way to Jerusalem, to your Cross and your Resurrection. Amen.

2027-03-21.title: Hosanna Sunday · The Lord's Entry into Jerusalem
readings: If these were silent, the stones would shout
The scepter shall not depart from Judah
The ark is brought to Jerusalem
Your king comes, humble, riding on a donkey
A great multitude with palm branches
Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes
2027-03-21.alt: Hosanna (Palm) Sunday. Holy Week (Hasho) begins this evening: special prayers and abstinence. In the 2025–26 lectionary this Sunday was also Social Welfare Day.
2027-03-21.verse: Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord—the King of Israel!
theo: Today Jesus enters Jerusalem, and the crowds go out to meet him with palm branches, shouting: “Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord—the King of Israel!” Zechariah had foretold it: “Lo, your king comes to you; triumphant and victorious is he, humble and riding on a donkey.” He comes as King, but not as the kings of this world: not on a war horse, but on a donkey, the animal of peace.

The Pharisees tell Jesus to silence his disciples. He answers: “I tell you, if these were silent, the stones would shout out.” All creation recognises its King. In our Malankara churches the palms are blessed and carried in procession, and we join the crowd of Jerusalem, and, as Revelation shows, the great multitude in heaven “robed in white, with palm branches in their hands”, crying: “Salvation belongs to our God… and to the Lamb!”

But we know where this road leads. The same city that shouts “Hosanna” will soon shout “Crucify him”. The King enters Jerusalem to be enthroned on the Cross. Genesis promised that “the scepter shall not depart from Judah”; the King from Judah reigns from the wood of the Cross. The ark of the covenant was brought into Jerusalem with joy and fear (2 Samuel 6); now the true Ark, God dwelling among us, enters the city.

Hosanna means “Save us, we pray.” It is a cry of praise and a cry for help. As Holy Week begins this evening, let us carry our palms home not as decorations but as a promise: Lord, I welcome you as my King; save me; and give me grace to follow you this week, through the Cross to the Resurrection.
conn: The humble king.
Zechariah 9:9 is fulfilled to the letter (John 12:15); his kingdom brings peace “from sea to sea” (Zechariah 9:10).
Palms in heaven.
Revelation 7:9: the palms of Jerusalem become the palms of the martyrs and saints before the Lamb.
The Lion of Judah.
Genesis 49:9–10: Judah the lion's whelp; the scepter shall not depart; Revelation 5:5 names Christ “the Lion of the tribe of Judah”.
Grafted in.
Romans 11:17: we Gentiles have been grafted into the olive tree of Israel; we too shout Hosanna to Israel's King.
altar: Every Holy Qurbono repeats the cry of Palm Sunday: “Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, Hosanna in the highest.” The One who entered Jerusalem enters our altar and our hearts.
outline: On a donkey, not a war horse: a kingdom of peace.
All creation recognises Christ; our praise must not fall silent.
The fickleness of the crowd, and of our hearts.
live: Keep Holy Week
Take part in the services of Pesaha, Good Friday, Holy Saturday and the Resurrection.
Keep your palm
Place the blessed palm by the cross at home and pray there each evening this week.
Make peace
Be reconciled with someone before Easter, as the King of peace enters your home.
fathers: St Andrew of Crete
“Let us run to accompany him as he hastens towards his passion… Let us spread before his feet not garments or branches, but ourselves” (Sermon 9 on Palm Sunday).
St Augustine

The Lord was King of Israel not to exact tribute or command armies, but to rule souls and bring them to the kingdom of heaven; it was no gain to the King of the ages to become King of men, but a sign of his mercy (Tractates on John 51).
magis: Catechism 559–560
Jesus enters Jerusalem as the Messiah, the Son of David, on a donkey; the Church's liturgy opens Holy Week with this feast.
Catechism 1352
The Sanctus with its Hosanna joins the Church's praise to the angels' song.
Catechism 571
The Paschal mystery of Christ's Cross and Resurrection stands at the centre of the Good News.
saints: Monday 22 to Wednesday 24 March: days of Holy Week. Thursday 25 March: Pesaha (Maundy Thursday); in 2027 this is also the date of the Annunciation, so check how your eparchy keeps it. Friday 26 March: Good Friday. Saturday 27 March: Holy Saturday. Sunday 28 March: Qyomtho, the Resurrection.
2027-03-21.prayer: Lord Jesus, humble King, you entered Jerusalem on a donkey to give your life for us. Hosanna: save us! As we carry our palms, give us faithful hearts that do not change from praise to rejection, and lead us through your Passion to the joy of your Resurrection. Amen.

2027-03-25.title: Pesaha · The Lord's Supper
readings: Let anyone who is thirsty come to me
Do not walk with those who lie in wait for blood
The Lord will reign on Mount Zion
The marriage supper of the Lamb
Do this in remembrance of me
2027-03-25.alt: Pesaha (Maundy Thursday). In 2027 the date of the Annunciation (25 March) falls on this day; follow the direction of your eparchy on how the Annunciation is kept.
2027-03-25.verse: Then he took a loaf of bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”
theo: On the night before he suffered, Jesus gathered his apostles in the upper room. “I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.” At that table he took bread, gave thanks, broke it and said: “This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.” And after supper he took the cup: “This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood.” On this night the Holy Qurbono was born.

Exodus tells of the first Passover: a lamb without blemish, its blood on the doorposts, eaten in haste by a people ready to leave slavery. “When I see the blood, I will pass over you.” Jesus is the true Passover Lamb. His blood marks us, his Body feeds us for the journey from slavery to freedom, from death to life.

At the same table Jesus gave his apostles a lesson in greatness: “Who is greater, the one who is at the table or the one who serves? Is it not the one at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.” In our tradition the washing of feet makes this visible. The Eucharist and service cannot be separated: the One who gives his Body washes our feet.

St Paul hands on what he received: “For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes.” He also warns against receiving unworthily. Pesaha is the night to thank God for the Holy Qurbono and the priesthood, to examine our hearts, and to stay awake with Jesus as he goes out to Gethsemane.
conn: The Passover lamb.
Exodus 12: the unblemished lamb whose blood saves; John 1:29 and 1 Corinthians 5:7: “Christ, our paschal lamb, has been sacrificed.”
The Day of Atonement.
Leviticus 16: the high priest enters the Holy of Holies with blood; Christ is priest and victim (Hebrews 9:11–14).
Rivers of living water.
John 7:37–38: from the heart of Christ flow streams of living water, fulfilled when his side is pierced (John 19:34).
The wedding supper of the Lamb.
Revelation 19:9: “Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb”: every Qurbono is a foretaste.
altar: Tonight we celebrate the Holy Qurbono at the very hour of its institution. The words the priest says over the bread and wine are the words of the upper room. Thank God tonight for every Qurbono you have received, and for the priests who celebrate it.
outline: The upper room: “I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you.”
From the lamb of Egypt to the Lamb of God.
The real presence: Christ gives himself.
The washing of feet: Eucharist and service.
Gethsemane: watch and pray with Jesus tonight.
live: Pesaha at home
Share the Pesaha appam and paal as a family, praying for unity and remembering the Last Supper.
Watch one hour
Spend time in adoration tonight, keeping Jesus company.
Serve someone
Do one humble service for a family member this week, as Jesus washed feet.
fathers: St Cyril of Jerusalem

“Since he himself has declared and said of the bread, This is my Body, who shall dare to doubt any longer? … Do not regard the bread and wine as simple elements, for they are, according to the Lord’s declaration, the Body and Blood of Christ” (Mystagogical Catecheses 4, 1 and 6).
St John Chrysostom

“It is not man who makes the gifts become the Body and Blood of Christ, but Christ himself, who was crucified for us. The priest stands there carrying out the action, but the power and grace are of God” (Homily on the Betrayal of Judas 1, 6).
magis: Catechism 1337–1340
The Lord instituted the Eucharist at the Last Supper as the memorial of his death and Resurrection, the new Passover.
Ecclesia de Eucharistia 3–5
The Church draws her life from the Eucharist; it was born in the upper room.
Catechism 1366–1367
The Eucharist is a sacrifice because it re-presents the sacrifice of the Cross.
saints: Friday 26 March: Good Friday (the collection is for the Holy Land). Saturday 27 March: Holy Saturday. Sunday 28 March: Qyomtho, the Resurrection.
2027-03-25.prayer: Lord Jesus, on the night you were betrayed you gave us your Body and Blood and washed your disciples' feet. Thank you for the Holy Qurbono and for the priesthood. Make us worthy to receive you, humble to serve one another, and faithful to stay with you in your agony. Amen.

2027-03-26.title: Good Friday · The Passion and Death of our Lord
readings: Readings of the Hours of Good Friday
Not listed in the Sacred Lectionary; follow the Hasho (Holy Week) book
The Gospels of the Passion read through the day
2027-03-26.alt: Good Friday. A day of fasting. The collection of the day is for the Holy Land, as directed by the Holy Father.
2027-03-26.verse: When Jesus had received the wine, he said, “It is finished.” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
theo: On Good Friday the Church stands at the foot of the Cross. The One who entered Jerusalem to the cry of Hosanna is condemned, mocked, scourged, crowned with thorns, and crucified outside the city between two criminals. The Holy One is counted among the wicked. The prophet had seen it long before: “He was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities… and by his bruises we are healed” (Isaiah 53:5).

From the Cross Jesus speaks words that the Church treasures. “Father, forgive them; for they do not know what they are doing.” To the repentant thief: “Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.” To his Mother and the beloved disciple: “Woman, here is your son… Here is your mother.” Then the cry of the abandoned: “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?” And at the end: “It is finished”, and “Father, into your hands I commend my spirit.”

“It is finished” is not a cry of defeat but of completion. The work the Father gave him is accomplished: the true Lamb has been sacrificed, the new covenant sealed in his blood. A soldier pierces his side, “and at once blood and water came out” (John 19:34). The Fathers saw in that blood and water the Eucharist and Baptism, the Church born from the side of Christ as Eve from the side of Adam.

On this day there is no Holy Qurbono in our tradition; the altar is bare because the Lamb himself is offered on the Cross. We venerate the Cross, we keep fast and silence, and we stand with Mary, who did not run away. The wood of shame has become the tree of life. “We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world.”
conn: The Suffering Servant.
Isaiah 52:13–53:12 describes the Passion centuries before it happened.
The tree of life.
The tree in Eden brought death; the tree of the Cross brings life (Genesis 2:9; Revelation 22:2).
The bronze serpent.
“As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up” (John 3:14; Numbers 21:9).
The new Adam's side.
As Eve was formed from Adam's side, the Church is born from the pierced side of Christ (John 19:34).
altar: Today the altar stands bare and there is no Holy Qurbono, for the one Sacrifice is contemplated on the Cross. Every Qurbono we celebrate makes present this same sacrifice of Calvary; today we simply kneel before it.
outline: Isaiah 53: by his bruises we are healed.
Point 2 · The words from the Cross
Forgiveness, Paradise, Mary, abandonment, completion, surrender.
The Church and the sacraments born from his side.
Do not run away; venerate the Cross.
“By your holy Cross you have redeemed the world.”
live: Keep the fast
Fast today with love, offering it for those who suffer.
Forgive (Luke 23:34)
Forgive one person today, as Jesus forgave from the Cross.
Venerate the Cross
Take part in the Good Friday service and kiss the Cross with gratitude.
fathers: St John Chrysostom
“There flowed from his side water and blood… the symbols of Baptism and the Mysteries. From these two the Church is born… as Eve was formed from the side of Adam” (Catechesis 3, 13–19).
St Cyril of Jerusalem
“He stretched out his hands on the Cross, that he might embrace the ends of the world; for Golgotha is the centre of the earth” (Catechetical Lectures 13, 28).
magis: Catechism 613–618
Christ's death is the Paschal sacrifice that accomplishes the definitive redemption of humanity; he offered himself freely.
Catechism 964
Mary's union with her Son in the work of salvation is shown at the foot of the Cross.
Catechism 766
The Church is born primarily of Christ's total self-giving: from the side of Christ asleep on the Cross.
saints: Saturday 27 March: Holy Saturday. Sunday 28 March: Qyomtho, the Resurrection.
2027-03-26.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, crucified for us, we adore you and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world. Forgive us, remember us in your kingdom, give us your Mother as our mother, and let us die with you to sin, that we may rise with you to life. Amen.

2027-03-27.title: Holy Saturday · The Lord Rests in the Tomb
readings: Hush! We must not mention the name of the Lord
Buried with him by baptism into death
The tomb is sealed and guarded
2027-03-27.alt: Holy Saturday. The Church waits at the tomb. In the night the celebration of the Resurrection begins.
2027-03-27.verse: So they went with the guard and made the tomb secure by sealing the stone.
theo: Holy Saturday is the day of great silence. The body of the Lord lies in the tomb of Joseph of Arimathea. The disciples are hidden in fear; the women wait for the sabbath to pass. His enemies, remembering his words about rising on the third day, ask Pilate for a guard; “so they went with the guard and made the tomb secure by sealing the stone.” They seal the tomb, not knowing that they are preparing witnesses to the Resurrection.

The Creed says: “he descended to the dead.” While his body rested in the tomb, Christ went down to the realm of the dead to bring the good news to the just who had waited for him, from Adam onwards. The Eastern Churches love the image of Christ breaking the gates of Sheol and taking Adam and Eve by the hand. Holy Saturday is not empty: it is the hidden victory.

St Paul explains what this means for us: “we have been buried with him by baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.” Our Baptism was a burial and a resurrection. Today we let die in us whatever must die, so that tonight we may rise with him.
Mary, his Mother, kept faith on this day when everyone else despaired. Let us keep this day in quiet prayer, with her, waiting in hope for the light of Qyomtho.
conn: The sign of Jonah.
“As Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so for three days and three nights the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth” (Matthew 12:40).
The sabbath rest.
God rested on the seventh day after creation (Genesis 2:2); Christ rests in the tomb on the sabbath after the work of the new creation.
Buried with him.
Romans 6:4: Baptism is our burial and resurrection with Christ.
The sealed stone.
The guards and the seal, meant to prevent a resurrection, become witnesses of it (Matthew 28:4, 11).
altar: The altar waits in silence; tonight it will be the place of the risen Lord. Like Mary, we keep watch, so that when the Qurbono of the Resurrection is celebrated our hearts are ready.
outline: Human power tries to keep God in the grave.
Point 2 · He descended to the dead
Christ brings light to Adam and the just of old.
Baptism: let the old self die.
“If we have died with him, we shall live with him.”
live: Keep silence
Spend part of today in quiet prayer, without television or phone.
Prepare for the night
Make your Easter Confession if you have not yet; prepare your home for the feast.
Pray with Mary
Pray the Sorrowful Mysteries or the Stabat Mater with her.
fathers: An ancient homily for Holy Saturday

“Something strange is happening: there is a great silence on earth… because the King is asleep. God has died in the flesh and has gone to rouse those who have slept ever since the world began… He took Adam by the hand: Awake, O sleeper” (ancient homily, read in the Liturgy of the Hours).
St Ephrem the Syrian
Death received him and was itself undone; Sheol could not hold him, and the dead heard his voice (Nisibene Hymns).
magis: Catechism 631–635
Jesus descended into the realm of the dead as Saviour, proclaiming the Good News to the spirits imprisoned there; this is the last phase of his messianic mission.
Catechism 624–630
Christ's burial: the mystery of Holy Saturday, when Christ lying in the tomb reveals God's great sabbath rest.
Catechism 1214–1215
Baptism signifies and actually brings about death to sin and entry into the life of the Trinity.
saints: Sunday 28 March: Qyomtho, the Resurrection of our Lord; Holy Qurbono for the people.
2027-03-27.prayer: Lord Jesus, you rested in the tomb and went down to those who sat in darkness. Bury with you all that is dead in us, keep us in hope with your Mother, and raise us with you to newness of life. Amen.

2027-03-28.title: Qyomtho · The Resurrection of our Lord
readings: He is not here; he has been raised
Daniel brought up from the lions' den
Peace, peace, to the far and the near
God raised this Jesus; we are witnesses
Christ died, was buried, and was raised
2027-03-28.alt: Qyomtho, Easter. Holy Qurbono for the people. The season of Qyomtho begins; this week is Hevoro (white) week.
2027-03-28.verse: He is not here; for he has been raised, as he said.
theo: Christ is risen! Very early on the first day of the week, the women go to the tomb, and an angel says: “Do not be afraid; I know that you are looking for Jesus who was crucified. He is not here; for he has been raised, as he said.” Then Jesus himself meets them: “Greetings!” They take hold of his feet and worship him. The One who was dead is alive for ever.

In John's Gospel Mary Magdalene runs to Peter and the beloved disciple; they run to the tomb and find the linen cloths lying there. The other disciple “saw and believed”. The empty tomb is not proof by itself, but it is the first sign; faith is born when we see with the heart that God has kept his word.

The Old Testament readings have prepared us. Daniel is brought up alive from the lions' den, because God shut the lions' mouths (Daniel 6:22). Moses sets up the tabernacle, and God's glory fills it. Isaiah announces: “Peace, peace, to the far and the near.” In the risen Christ the glory of God dwells among us for ever, and his first word to the disciples will be: “Peace be with you.”

St Peter preaches on the day of Pentecost: “This Jesus God raised up, and of that all of us are witnesses.” St Paul hands on the heart of the Gospel: “Christ died for our sins in accordance with the scriptures… he was buried… he was raised on the third day.” Easter is not a beautiful story; it is the event on which everything stands. Because Christ is risen, sin is forgiven, death is defeated, and our own bodies will rise. Let us live as Easter people.
conn: Daniel and the lions.
Daniel, sealed in the den with a stone (Daniel 6:17), comes out alive at dawn: a figure of the sealed tomb and the risen Lord.
The tabernacle.
Exodus 40: God's dwelling is set up on the first day of the first month; the risen body of Christ is the true temple (John 2:19–21).
Peace to the far and the near.
Isaiah 57:19 and Ephesians 2:17: the risen Christ preaches peace to all.
The third day.
Hosea 6:2 and Jonah 1:17: the third day of God's saving action.
altar: Every Sunday is a little Easter, and every Holy Qurbono is the meeting with the risen Lord. As the women held his feet, we receive his risen Body. Today let us receive him with Easter joy.
outline: Christ is risen! He is risen indeed!
“He is not here; he has been raised, as he said.” God keeps his word.
The women, Mary Magdalene, Peter and John: faith is born.
Peter: “we are witnesses”; we too are sent.
Sin forgiven, death defeated, hope for the body; live it this week.
“He is not here; he is risen!”
live: Greet with Easter joy
Greet family and friends with “Christ is risen!” throughout Easter week.
Visit someone sad
Bring Easter joy to a sick, elderly or grieving person.
Keep the Sundays
Resolve to keep every Sunday as a little Easter: Qurbono, rest, family.
fathers: St John Chrysostom

“Let no one fear death, for the Saviour's death has set us free… Christ is risen, and the demons are fallen; Christ is risen, and the angels rejoice; Christ is risen, and life reigns” (Paschal Homily).
St Ephrem the Syrian
“Glory to you, who put on our body and went down to Sheol, and rose and raised us with you” (Nisibene Hymns).
magis: Catechism 638–658
The Resurrection of Christ is the crowning truth of our faith; it is a real, historical event with a transcendent character, confirming all that Christ taught.
Catechism 1169
Easter is the “feast of feasts”, the “solemnity of solemnities”.
Catechism 989–990
We firmly believe that, as Christ is truly risen, the righteous will live for ever with him and he will raise them up on the last day.
saints: The week after Qyomtho is kept with joy. Next Sunday: New Sunday (the appearance to Thomas).
2027-03-28.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you have trampled down death by death and given life to those in the tombs. Fill us with Easter joy and peace, make us witnesses of your Resurrection, and raise us with you on the last day. Christ is risen! He is truly risen! Amen.

quick: Jesus sees the bent woman and sets her free.
God's sabbath rest is our freedom and healing.
Healed ourselves, we become Good Samaritans.
2027-03-07.action: Stop for one person in need you would usually pass by.
2027-03-07.question: What has bent me down, and do I let Jesus lift me up?
2027-03-07.special: K'piphtho Sunday, fifth Sunday of the Great Fast.
illus: An old woman in a Kerala village had walked bent for years with a back problem. After an operation she stood straight and said with tears: “I can see the sky again.” Sin and sorrow can bend the soul in the same way.

family.explain: A woman could not stand up straight for eighteen years. Jesus touched her, and she stood up straight and praised God!
family.intention: We pray for people who carry heavy burdens and for all who are sick.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we help this week, like the Good Samaritan?”

catechism: The sabbath and works of mercy.
kidsaint: The Forty Martyrs of Sebaste (9 Mar)

Forty Christian soldiers in Armenia who were made to stand on a frozen lake because they would not give up Jesus. They encouraged one another and stayed faithful together. Lesson: help your friends stay faithful.
term: K'piphtho means “the bent (crippled) woman”. The fifth Sunday of the Great Fast reads her healing (Luke 13:10–17).
termMore: The Syriac and Greek Fathers read the parable as the story of salvation: humanity wounded on the road, Christ the Samaritan, the oil and wine of the sacraments, the inn of the Church.

quick: Jesus is the light of the world: he opens blind eyes.
Faith grows step by step: “Lord, I believe.”
Bartimaeus receives sight and follows Jesus on the way.
2027-03-14.action: Pray often this week: “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me.”
2027-03-14.question: Where am I still blind, and do I want to see?
2027-03-14.special: Samio Sunday, sixth Sunday of the Great Fast. Announce the Fortieth Friday (19 Mar), Lazarus Saturday (20 Mar) and Hosanna Sunday (21 Mar); remind the faithful to bring palm leaves and flowers.
illus: Free eye camps in Kerala villages give sight to hundreds every year. One old man, after his cataract operation, said: “Now I can see my grandchildren's faces.” Jesus came to give us a sight even greater: to see God's face in Christ.

family.explain: A blind man called Bartimaeus shouted to Jesus for help. Jesus asked what he wanted, and he said: “I want to see!” Jesus healed him, and he followed Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for the blind and for those who have lost faith.
family.ask: Ask: “How will our family keep Holy Week this year?”

kidsaint: The husband of Mary and the foster father of Jesus, a carpenter who worked hard, protected his family and obeyed God at once. Lesson: work well and take care of your family.
term: Samio is Syriac for “the blind man”. The sixth Sunday of the Great Fast, the last before Hosanna Sunday, reads the healing of the blind.
termMore: The Fortieth Friday and Lazarus Saturday

On the Friday before Hosanna Sunday the forty days of the Fast are completed (the lectionary notes no fasting or prostrations that day). The next day remembers the raising of Lazarus, and Holy Week follows.

quick: Hosanna: the humble King enters Jerusalem on a donkey.
If we are silent, the stones will shout.
Hosanna means “Save us”: enter Holy Week with Christ.
2027-03-21.action: Take part in every service of Holy Week this year.
2027-03-21.question: Will my Hosanna today still be faithful on Friday?
2027-03-21.special: Hosanna (Palm) Sunday: blessing of palms and procession. Holy Week begins this evening; remind the faithful about the special prayers and abstinence. (In 2025–26 also Social Welfare Day; check the collection.)
illus: In Kerala, children carry the blessed tender palm leaves home and their grandmothers weave them into small crosses for the door. The palm that welcomed the King becomes the sign of his Cross. That is Holy Week in one leaf.

family.explain: Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a little donkey. People waved palm branches and shouted “Hosanna!” They welcomed him as their King.
family.intention: We pray that our family may keep Holy Week well and welcome Jesus as King.
family.ask: Ask: “Which services of Holy Week will we attend together?”

kidsaint: When Jesus entered the city, children in the Temple kept shouting “Hosanna to the Son of David!” Jesus said that God had prepared praise from the mouths of children (Matthew 21:15–16). Lesson: your praise matters to Jesus.
term: Hosanna is Hebrew for “Save us, we pray”. On the Sunday before Easter the Church blesses palms and celebrates the Lord's entry into Jerusalem; Holy Week (Hasho) begins in the evening.
termMore: The palms are kept at home through the year; in the Malankara tradition they may be brought back and used in the fire of the Yaldo night service, so that the same palms that welcomed the King greet his birth.

quick: On this night Jesus gave us the Holy Qurbono.
He is the true Passover Lamb who saves us.
The One who gives his Body washes our feet: Eucharist and service.
2027-03-25.action: Spend time in adoration tonight, keeping Jesus company.
2027-03-25.question: How do I prepare to receive the Lord's Body and Blood?
2027-03-25.special: Pesaha (Maundy Thursday): Holy Qurbono of the Lord's Supper and the washing of the feet. In 2027 also the date of the Annunciation; follow the eparchy's direction.
illus: On Pesaha night St Thomas Christian families gather around the table, and the eldest breaks the Pesaha appam marked with a cross and shares it with everyone, even those away abroad who are remembered by name. The whole family becomes an upper room.

family.explain: On the night before he died, Jesus had a special meal with his friends. He took bread and said, “This is my body,” and the cup, “This is my blood.” That is how he gave us Holy Qurbana.
family.intention: We thank God for the Holy Qurbono and pray for our priests.
family.ask: Ask: “What can each of us do to serve someone in our family this week?”

kidsaint: The youngest apostle, who rested his head on Jesus' chest at the Last Supper and later stood at the foot of the Cross with Mary. Lesson: stay close to Jesus, especially when it is hard.
term: From the Hebrew for “Passover”. Maundy Thursday, when the Lord instituted the Holy Qurbono and washed the disciples' feet. Kerala Christian families break the Pesaha appam at home in the evening.
termMore: At the Pesaha service the bishop or priest washes the feet of twelve persons, as Jesus did (John 13:1–15), showing that the Eucharist leads to humble service.

quick: “He was wounded for our transgressions.”
From the Cross: forgiveness, Paradise, and Mary given to us.
“It is finished”: the work of salvation is complete.
2027-03-26.action: Forgive one person today, as Jesus forgave from the Cross.
2027-03-26.question: What does the Cross ask of me today?
2027-03-26.special: Good Friday: day of fasting; no Holy Qurbono; veneration of the Cross. Collection for the Holy Land.
illus: In many Kerala homes on Good Friday the television is switched off, the family eats only kanji, and an old crucifix is placed on the table. The children ask why. A grandmother answers: “Because today Jesus died for you.”

family.explain: Jesus died on the cross because he loves us. Even on the cross he forgave the people who hurt him, and he promised heaven to the thief who asked for mercy.
family.intention: We pray for all who are suffering, and we thank Jesus for his love.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone I need to forgive today?”

catechism: Mary at the foot of the Cross.
kidsaint: One of the men crucified beside Jesus said: “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.” Jesus promised: “Today you will be with me in Paradise.” (Later tradition calls him Dismas.) Lesson: it is never too late to turn to Jesus.
term: The day of the Lord's Passion and death. In the Malankara tradition the long service of the Hours is prayed, the Cross is venerated and then laid to rest, recalling the burial of the Lord, and the faithful keep fast.
termMore: Because on this day, through the suffering of Christ, the greatest good was done: the redemption of the world. In Malayalam it is called the Friday of sorrow; both names are true.

quick: Holy Saturday: the great silence; the Lord rests in the tomb.
He descended to the dead to free Adam and the just of old.
Buried with him in Baptism, we wait to rise with him.
2027-03-27.action: Spend part of today in silent prayer.
2027-03-27.question: What in me must be buried, so that I can rise with Christ?
2027-03-27.special: Holy Saturday: the Church waits at the tomb; preparation for the night of the Resurrection.
illus: On Holy Saturday Kerala homes are quiet: the kitchen prepares the Easter meal, but no one plays loud music. Children are told: “Jesus is in the tomb; tonight he will rise.” The whole house waits.

family.explain: After Jesus died, his friends laid him in a tomb and rolled a big stone in front. His enemies sealed it and put guards there. But they could not stop what God was going to do!
family.intention: We pray for people who are sad and have lost hope.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we get ready for Easter together?”

kidsaint: A rich and respected man who was a secret disciple of Jesus. After Jesus died, he bravely asked Pilate for his body and laid him in his own new tomb. Lesson: be brave to show your love for Jesus.
term: The day between the Cross and the Resurrection, when Christ rests in the tomb and descends to the dead. It is kept in silence and prayer; the celebration of Qyomtho begins in the night.
termMore: An article of the Creed: after his death Christ went to the realm of the dead (Sheol) not to suffer but to free the righteous who had gone before him (1 Peter 3:18–19; 4:6).

quick: Christ is risen: “He is not here; he has been raised.”
The empty tomb and the meeting with the risen Lord give birth to faith.
Because Christ is risen, death is defeated: live as Easter people.
2027-03-28.action: Greet everyone with “Christ is risen!” throughout this week.
2027-03-28.question: What difference does the Resurrection make to my life this week?
2027-03-28.special: Qyomtho, the Resurrection of our Lord: day of obligation; Holy Qurbono for the people. Hevoro week follows.
illus: On Easter night in Kerala the church bells ring after weeks of silence, the people light candles from the paschal flame, and the dark church fills with light. A child once asked: “Did Jesus switch on the lights?” In a way, yes: he lit up the world.

family.explain: On Easter morning the women went to Jesus' tomb, but it was empty! An angel said: “He is risen!” Then Jesus himself met them. Jesus is alive for ever!
family.intention: We thank God for Easter joy and pray for all who are sad or sick.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we share Easter joy with someone this week?”

kidsaint: She stayed at the Cross and came first to the tomb on Easter morning. The risen Jesus called her by name and sent her to tell the apostles. Lesson: tell others that Jesus is alive!
term: Syriac for “resurrection”. The feast of feasts, the Resurrection of our Lord, and the season of fifty days that follows until Pentecost.
termMore: The week after Easter, called Hevoro (white) week, recalling the white garments of the newly baptised and the joy of the Resurrection.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today Jesus sees a woman in the synagogue who has been bent over for eighteen years. For eighteen years she has looked only at the ground. Jesus calls her and says: “Woman, you are set free from your ailment.” He lays his hands on her, and immediately she stands up straight and praises God.

The leader of the synagogue is angry: healing is work, and the sabbath is for rest. Jesus replies: you untie your ox and your donkey on the sabbath to lead them to water. Should not this daughter of Abraham, bound for eighteen years, be set free on the sabbath? God's day is the day of freedom.

Many of us are bent in some way: by guilt, by worry, by an addiction, by grief, by carrying everything alone. We get used to looking at the ground. In this Fast Jesus calls us by name, lays his hands on us in Confession and in the Holy Qurbono, and says: stand up, look up, you are free.

And the evening Gospel tells us what to do once we are healed. The Good Samaritan saw a wounded man, was moved with pity, and bound up his wounds. Jesus says: “Go and do likewise.” This week, stop for someone you would usually pass by. Let us be healed, and become healers. Amen.
kids: Children, try bending over and looking only at the floor. Not nice, is it? A woman in the Bible had to walk like that for eighteen years!
Jesus saw her, called her, and touched her. And she stood up straight and praised God!
Jesus also told a story about a man who stopped to help someone hurt on the road. Let's help others too. Let's say: “Jesus, help me to help others!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on the last Sunday before Holy Week we hear of two blind men who receive their sight. In John's Gospel a man blind from birth; in Mark's, Bartimaeus, a beggar sitting by the road at Jericho.

Jesus makes clay, anoints the blind man's eyes and sends him to wash in the pool of Siloam, which means “Sent”. He comes back seeing. Then come the questions, the arguments, the threats. He does not know how to answer the scholars, but he knows one thing: “I was blind; now I see.” And his faith grows until he kneels and says: “Lord, I believe.” Meanwhile those who are sure they see refuse the light.

Bartimaeus cannot see, but he can shout. “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” People tell him to be quiet. He shouts louder. Jesus stops and asks: “What do you want me to do for you?” “Teacher, let me see again.” He receives his sight and follows Jesus on the road, the road to Jerusalem.

Next Sunday is Hosanna. Holy Week begins. Let us ask Jesus to heal our blindness: to the poor beside us, to our own sins, to God's love. Let us pray Bartimaeus' prayer all through this week. And having received our sight, let us follow Jesus on the way, to his Cross and his Resurrection. Amen.
kids: Children, close your eyes for a moment. Now open them! It's wonderful to see, isn't it? Bartimaeus was blind. He heard Jesus was passing and shouted: “Jesus, help me!”
People said, “Be quiet!” But he shouted even louder. Jesus asked: “What do you want?” “I want to see!” And Jesus gave him his sight!
Next week we will wave palms for Jesus. Let's say: “Jesus, open my eyes to see you!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we carry palms like the crowds of Jerusalem. Jesus rides into the holy city, and the people go out to meet him shouting: “Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!” The prophet Zechariah had said: your King comes to you, humble, riding on a donkey.

Notice how he comes. Not on a war horse, like a conqueror, but on a donkey, the animal of ordinary people and of peace. He is a King, but his throne will be a cross and his crown will be thorns. When the Pharisees want the crowd silenced, Jesus says: “If these were silent, the stones would shout out.” All creation knows its King.

But the same city that cries “Hosanna” today will cry “Crucify him” on Friday. How quickly hearts change. And our hearts too: we praise him on Sunday and forget him on Monday. Holy Week is the time to ask for faithful hearts, hearts that keep shouting Hosanna even at the foot of the Cross.

Hosanna means “Save us, we pray.” Let us take our palms home not as decorations but as a promise: Lord, you are my King; save me. Come to all the services of this Holy Week. Walk with Jesus from the upper room to Calvary, and on to the empty tomb. Hosanna in the highest! Amen.
kids: Children, today we wave our palms like the children of Jerusalem! Jesus came riding on a little donkey, and everyone shouted: “Hosanna! Hosanna!”
Jesus is a King, but a gentle King of peace. This week we will remember how much he loved us: he gave his life on the cross, and then he rose again!
Take your palm home and put it near the cross. Let's shout together: “Hosanna to Jesus our King!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, tonight we enter the upper room. Jesus says: “I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.” He knew what was coming: betrayal, arrest, the Cross. And on that night he gave us his greatest gift.

“He took bread, gave thanks, broke it and gave it to them, saying: This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.” And the cup: “This cup is the new covenant in my blood.” The lamb of the first Passover saved Israel from death; Jesus, the true Lamb, gives himself to save the whole world. Every Holy Qurbono since that night is this same gift.

And at the same table Jesus taught them how to be great: “I am among you as one who serves.” He knelt and washed their feet. We cannot receive the Body of Christ and refuse to serve the body of Christ in our brothers and sisters. The altar and the towel belong together.

Tonight, at home, families will break the Pesaha appam. Let it be a real family communion: forgive one another, remember those far away, thank God for the Qurbono and for our priests. And after supper, do not leave Jesus alone. Stay with him, as he goes out to pray in Gethsemane. Amen.
kids: Children, tonight is Pesaha. The night before Jesus died, he had a special supper with his friends. He took bread and said: “This is my body.” He took the cup and said: “This is my blood.” That was the first Holy Qurbana!
Then Jesus knelt down and washed his friends' feet, like a servant. He wanted to teach them to love and help one another.
Tonight at home, help someone without being asked. Let's say: “Thank you, Jesus, for giving us yourself!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today we stand at the foot of the Cross. The One who was welcomed with Hosanna on Sunday is today mocked, scourged, crowned with thorns and nailed to a cross between two criminals. Isaiah had seen it: “He was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; by his bruises we are healed.”

Listen to his words from the Cross. “Father, forgive them; for they do not know what they are doing.” He forgives those who are killing him. To the thief who asks to be remembered, he promises: “Today you will be with me in Paradise.” To his Mother and the beloved disciple he says: “Here is your son; here is your mother.” He gives us his own Mother.

And then: “It is finished.” Not “I am finished”, but “It is accomplished.” The work of salvation is complete. The soldier's spear opens his side, and blood and water flow: the Fathers saw there the Eucharist and Baptism, the Church born from the heart of Christ.

Today there is no Qurbono; the altar is bare. We kneel before the Cross, we fast, we keep silence, and we stand with Mary who did not run away. Let each of us forgive someone today, as he forgave. We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world. Amen.
kids: Children, today is Good Friday. Jesus died on the cross. He let it happen because he loves us so much and wanted to take away our sins.
On the cross Jesus forgave the people who hurt him. He told a thief who was sorry: “Today you will be with me in heaven.”
Today let's be quiet, pray, and say sorry to anyone we have hurt. Let's say: “Thank you, Jesus, for loving me so much!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is the day of the great silence. The Lord's body lies in the tomb. The disciples hide in fear. The stone is sealed and soldiers stand guard. It seems that death has won.

But the ancient Church sang a different song. While his body rested, Christ descended to the dead, to Adam and Eve, to Abraham and the prophets, to all who had waited for him. An old homily imagines him taking Adam by the hand: “Awake, O sleeper, and arise from the dead.” Holy Saturday is not empty; it is the hidden victory.

St Paul tells us that in Baptism we were buried with Christ, so that we might rise with him. Today is a good day to bury with him whatever is dead in us: a sin we keep returning to, a grudge, a fear. Bring it to the tomb, and leave it there.

And let us stay with Mary. On this day, when everyone else despaired, she kept faith. Let us keep silence, prepare our hearts and our homes, and wait for the night when the stone will be rolled away. Amen.
kids: Children, today Jesus' body is resting in the tomb. A big stone is in front, and soldiers are guarding it. Everyone is quiet and sad.
But Mary, Jesus' mother, kept trusting God. And tonight something wonderful will happen!
Today let's be quiet and get ready for Easter. Let's say: “Jesus, I'm waiting for you!”

homily: Christ is risen! He is risen indeed! Dear brothers and sisters, very early this morning the women went to the tomb with spices, expecting to anoint a dead body. Instead they found an angel who said: “Do not be afraid. He is not here; for he has been raised, as he said.”

As he said. On the road to Jerusalem Jesus had told his disciples three times that he would suffer, die and rise on the third day. They did not understand. Today God has kept his word. And Jesus himself meets the women: “Greetings!” They hold his feet and worship him. Peter and John run to the tomb; the beloved disciple “saw and believed”.

St Paul gives us the heart of the Gospel: “Christ died for our sins, he was buried, and he was raised on the third day.” Because Christ is risen, our sins can be forgiven; because Christ is risen, death is not the end; because Christ is risen, the graves of our loved ones are not the last word. Daniel came out of the lions' den at dawn; Christ came out of the tomb, and he will bring us out too.

St Peter said: “God raised this Jesus, and we are all witnesses.” Now we are the witnesses. Let us live as Easter people: joyful, forgiving, hopeful. Bring this joy to someone who is sad this week. Christ is risen! He is truly risen! Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Say it with me: He is risen indeed!
On Sunday morning the women went to Jesus' tomb and found it empty. An angel said: “He is not here, he is risen!” Then Jesus himself came to meet them. They were so happy!
Jesus is alive for ever, and he is with us. Today tell everyone at home: “Jesus is alive!” Let's shout: “Alleluia!”

intro: For eighteen years a woman had been bent over, unable to look up. Jesus sees her, calls her, lays his hands on her, and she stands straight and praises God. The evening Gospel adds the Good Samaritan: we too must stoop to lift others.

sub: She could not stand up straight for eighteen years; many carry invisible burdens for years.
Sin, grief, debt, illness, addiction can bend us so that we only look at the ground.
Like Ben Sira, we can cry to the Lord as Father in the days of trouble.
q: I cried out, “Lord, you are my Father; do not forsake me in the days of trouble, when there is no help against the proud.”
Just then there appeared a woman with a spirit that had crippled her for eighteen years. She was bent over and was quite unable to stand up straight.
points.apply: Name the burden that bends you, and bring it to Christ in prayer and confession.

points.h: Jesus sees, calls and lifts up
sub: She does not ask; Jesus sees her first and calls her.
He lays his hands on her: his touch restores dignity.
She stands upright and praises God; the Lord lifts up those who are bowed down.
q: The LORD opens the eyes of the blind. The LORD lifts up those who are bowed down; the LORD loves the righteous.
When Jesus saw her, he called her over and said, “Woman, you are set free from your ailment.” When he laid his hands on her, immediately she stood up straight and began praising God.
points.apply: Thank God for a time he lifted you up; tell someone about it.

sub: The Law commanded: love your neighbour as yourself.
The Samaritan saw, was moved with pity, came near, bandaged and cared.
Each of us is called to stoop and lift others, especially the forgotten.
q: You shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
He said, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus said to him, “Go and do likewise.”
points.apply: Help one person this week who is “bent over”: sick, elderly, poor or discouraged.

concl: Christ lifts up the bowed down and sends us to do the same.
This Great Fast, let him straighten us, and let us become good Samaritans.
2027-03-07.resolve: Visit or call one person who has been suffering for a long time.

intro: Theme: “I was blind, now I see.”

The Gospel of the man born blind is a journey from darkness to light, from not seeing to believing and worshipping. It is also our story: Baptism is called “illumination”, and Lent prepares us to see Christ more clearly.

sub: The disciples ask: who sinned, this man or his parents?
Jesus refuses that easy answer: God's works will be revealed in him.
Isaiah promised a day when the eyes of the blind would be opened: Christ brings that day.
q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
Jesus answered, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned; he was born blind so that God's works might be revealed in him.”
points.apply: Never judge the suffering of others as God's punishment; offer help instead.

points.h: Go and wash: the light of Baptism
sub: Jesus makes mud, anoints the man's eyes, and sends him to the pool of Siloam, “Sent”.
He obeys, washes and comes back seeing: an image of Baptism, the sacrament of enlightenment.
Solomon prayed for an understanding mind; true sight is to see as God sees.
q: Give your servant therefore an understanding mind to govern your people, able to discern between good and evil.
“Go, wash in the pool of Siloam” (which means Sent). Then he went and washed and came back able to see.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal faith: pray the Creed slowly each day this week.

points.h: From sight to faith and worship
sub: Questioned and expelled, the man holds to what he knows: “I was blind, now I see.”
Meeting Jesus again, he believes and worships: “Lord, I believe.”
Like Job, he moves from hearing about God to seeing him; like Bartimaeus, he follows Jesus on the way.
q: I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
One thing I do know, that though I was blind, now I see. … He said, “Lord, I believe.” And he worshiped him.
points.apply: Share your simple testimony with someone: what Christ has done for you.

concl: Christ is the light of the world. The real blindness is to refuse to see him.
Let us wash, believe and worship, and walk as children of light toward Easter.
2027-03-14.resolve: Spend fifteen minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week, asking: “Lord, let me see.”

intro: Holy Week begins with palms and songs. Jesus enters Jerusalem as King, but on a donkey, and he weeps over the city. The same crowd that sings “Hosanna” will soon cry “Crucify”. Where do we stand?

sub: Zechariah foretold a king, triumphant yet humble, riding on a donkey.
Jesus does not come on a war horse; his kingdom is peace.
He wants to enter our hearts, homes and city not by force but by love.
q: Lo, your king comes to you; triumphant and victorious is he, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
So they took branches of palm trees and went out to meet him, shouting, “Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord—the King of Israel!”
points.apply: Keep your blessed palm in a place of honour at home, and welcome Christ as King of your family.

sub: “Hosanna” means “Save us”: the cry of the Psalm sung by pilgrims.
Jesus weeps over the city that did not recognise the things that make for peace.
Our Hosanna must last beyond Sunday, through Good Friday.
q: Save us, we beseech you, O LORD! O LORD, we beseech you, give us success! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the LORD.
As he came near and saw the city, he wept over it, saying, “If you, even you, had only recognized on this day the things that make for peace!”
points.apply: Take part in all the services of Holy Week: Pesaha, Good Friday, Holy Saturday and Easter.

sub: Jacob foretold a ruler from Judah to whom the nations would bow.
St John sees a countless multitude from every nation, robed in white, with palms in their hands.
The palms we carry today point to the victory of the Lamb in heaven.
q: The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until tribute comes to him; and the obedience of the peoples is his.

There was a great multitude that no one could count, from every nation, from all tribes and peoples and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, robed in white, with palm branches in their hands.
points.apply: Pray for persecuted Christians, who carry the palm of faithfulness today.

concl: The King enters Jerusalem to give his life. His throne will be a Cross, his crown thorns, his victory the Resurrection.
Let us follow him this week, not as a fickle crowd but as faithful disciples.
2027-03-21.resolve: Read the Passion narrative (John 18–19) with your family during Holy Week.

intro: Theme: “This is my body, given for you.”
On this holy night Jesus eats the Passover with his disciples, gives us the Holy Qurbono and the priesthood, and washes their feet. Everything we are as a Church flows from this Upper Room.

sub: In Egypt the blood of the lamb on the doorposts saved the people from death.
Jesus takes bread and the cup: his body given, his blood poured out, the new covenant.
He is the Lamb whose blood marks us in Baptism and feeds us in the Qurbono.
q: The blood shall be a sign for you on the houses where you live: when I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague shall destroy you.

Then he took a loaf of bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body, which is given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.” And he did the same with the cup after supper, saying, “This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood.”
points.apply: Receive Holy Communion tonight with deep faith that it is truly the Lord.

sub: Isaiah foresaw a feast for all peoples on God's mountain.
St John hears: “Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.”
Every Qurbono is a foretaste of that eternal banquet, and Jesus made his apostles priests to celebrate it.
q: On this mountain the LORD of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of well-aged wines.
And the angel said to me, “Write this: Blessed are those who are invited to the marriage supper of the Lamb.”
points.apply: Pray tonight for your priests, and for vocations to the priesthood.

sub: Abraham welcomed strangers: “Let a little water be brought, and wash your feet.”
Jesus, Lord and Teacher, kneels and washes his disciples' feet.
The Eucharist and service cannot be separated: whoever receives the Lord must serve the brethren.
q: Let a little water be brought, and wash your feet, and rest yourselves under the tree.
So if I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet. For I have set you an example, that you also should do as I have done to you.
points.apply: Do one humble service at home tonight or tomorrow, especially for someone you find difficult.

concl: Jesus loved his own to the end. In the bread and the cup he gives himself; in the basin and towel he shows how to love.
Let us receive him with faith, adore him with gratitude, and serve one another with humility.
2027-03-25.resolve: Stay with the Lord in prayer for an hour tonight, as he asked his disciples.

intro: Today we stand at the Cross with Mary and John. We do not only remember a death; we contemplate the love that saved the world. Three words guide us: he bore our sins, he cried out in our abandonment, he is the Lamb God provided.

points.h: He was wounded for our transgressions
sub: Isaiah saw the suffering Servant, crushed for our iniquities.
Jesus carries not his own sin but ours; by his wounds we are healed.
“It is finished”: not defeat but accomplishment; the work of salvation is complete.
q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
When Jesus had received the wine, he said, “It is finished.” Then he bowed his head and gave up his spirit.
points.apply: Look at the crucifix today and say: “Lord, you did this for me.”

sub: Jesus prays the words of Psalm 22: “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
He enters even our experience of God's absence, so that no one is ever alone again.
The Psalm that begins in anguish ends in trust and praise.
q: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me, from the words of my groaning?
And about three o'clock Jesus cried with a loud voice, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” that is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”
points.apply: Bring to the Cross someone who feels abandoned, and pray for them by name.

sub: Abraham told Isaac: “God himself will provide the lamb.”
At the Cross God provides his own Son.
A Roman centurion, seeing how Jesus died, confesses: “Truly this man was God's Son!”
q: Abraham said, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.”
Now when the centurion and those with him, who were keeping watch over Jesus, saw the earthquake and what took place, they were terrified and said, “Truly this man was God's Son!”
points.apply: Venerate the Cross with love today, and keep the fast faithfully.

concl: From the pierced side flowed blood and water: the sacraments of the Church.
Let us remain at the Cross with Mary, in silence and gratitude, waiting in hope for the third day.
2027-03-26.resolve: Keep silence and avoid entertainment from noon to three o'clock today.

intro: Theme: “The great silence of the sealed tomb.”

Holy Saturday is the day of silence. The Lord rests in the tomb; the stone is sealed and guarded. Yet the Church professes that he descended to the dead to set free the just who had gone before him (CCC 632–635). We wait, as Mary waited, in faith.

points.h: The tomb is sealed, but God is not
sub: The authorities seal the stone and post a guard, afraid of the third day.
The Psalmist trusted that God would not let his faithful one see corruption.
Human seals cannot hold the Lord of life.
q: For you do not give me up to Sheol, or let your faithful one see the Pit.
So they went with the guard and made the tomb secure by sealing the stone.
points.apply: Name the “sealed tomb” in your life where you have lost hope, and entrust it to Christ.

sub: Hosea foretold: on the third day he will raise us up.
Jesus himself gave the sign: as Jonah three days in the fish, so the Son of Man in the heart of the earth.
His rest in the tomb is not the end; it is the night before the dawn.
q: After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up, that we may live before him.
For just as Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the sea monster, so for three days and three nights the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth.
points.apply: Spend some time today in quiet waiting, without noise or screens.

points.h: Buried with him, to rise with him
sub: Ezekiel saw God opening graves and bringing his people home.
In Baptism we were buried with Christ so that we might walk in newness of life.
The grain of wheat must die to bear fruit; our dying to sin prepares Easter joy.
q: I am going to open your graves, and bring you up from your graves, O my people; and I will bring you back to the land of Israel.
Therefore we have been buried with him by baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.
points.apply: Prepare to renew your baptismal promises at Easter: renounce sin and profess the faith.

concl: Holy Saturday teaches us to wait in faith when God seems silent.
Tomorrow the stone will be rolled away. Let us keep vigil with Mary, Mother of hope.
2027-03-27.resolve: Pray with Mary tonight: the Rosary or the Sorrowful Mysteries, waiting for the Resurrection.

intro: Theme: “He is not here; he has been raised.”

Christ is risen! This is the feast of feasts. Everything in our faith depends on it: if Christ has not been raised, our faith is futile; but Christ has been raised. Today we celebrate the victory over death, the witness of the empty tomb, and our mission to proclaim it.

sub: Isaiah promised: God will swallow up death forever and wipe away every tear.
Peter proclaims: it was impossible for death to hold him.
The Resurrection is not a return to ordinary life but the beginning of new creation.
q: He will swallow up death forever. Then the Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from all faces.
But God raised him up, having freed him from death, because it was impossible for him to be held in its power.
points.apply: Bring your grief to the Risen Lord and let him wipe away your tears.

points.h: The empty tomb: he saw and believed
sub: Daniel came out of the lions' den unharmed because he trusted in God.
Mary Magdalene finds the stone rolled away; the beloved disciple enters, sees the linen and believes.
Faith in the Resurrection rests on the witness of those who saw the empty tomb and the risen Lord.
q: Daniel was taken up out of the den, and no kind of harm was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.
Then the other disciple, who reached the tomb first, also went in, and he saw and believed.
points.apply: Profess the Creed today with special faith: “On the third day he rose again.”

sub: The angel says: “Do not be afraid”; Jesus says the same.
The women are sent to the apostles: the first announcers of Easter.
“Arise, shine”: every Christian is sent to bring Easter joy to the world.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
Then Jesus said to them, “Do not be afraid; go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee; there they will see me.”
points.apply: Greet your family and neighbours today with “Christ is risen!” and share the joy with someone who is sad or alone.

concl: The tomb is empty, death is defeated, and the Lord is alive.
Let us live as Easter people: without fear, full of hope, witnesses of the Risen One.
2027-03-28.resolve: During the fifty days of Easter, greet others with “Christ is risen” and pray the Glory Be with special joy.
